text:
jess: heads-up — spotted a canary that blew past quota despite the org limit. looks like service-account claims are being resolved twice during routing and the attribution falls back to the SA instead of the originating project.

oliver: ugh. is this during delegated tokens or cross-project SA impersonation?

jess: delegated tokens. sequence: customer app -> project A mint -> project B SA -> runtime. the final effective project used by quota worker is the SA's project. so usage counts against B instead of A.

dina: that sounds like a claims propagation ordering bug. we should canonicalize "origin" claim earlier in the auth pipeline and stash a single source-of-truth header for routing/quotas.

samir: agree. proposal: add an immutable header `x-origin-project` at mint time and have the routing layer prefer it over derived SA claims. simple patch:

```
# mint service
headers['x-origin-project'] = claims.get('origin_project') or claims.get('iss')
```

leo: UI question — if we change attribution logic, how will the Console display it? customers will panic if they see charges move between projects without explanation. we need a visual breadcrumb: "reported-by / effective-attributed-to" with a hover explaining fallback.

jess: yep. proposal for console: show two columns in the request inspector: origin_project and effective_project. if they differ, show a small warning + a link to the rollout notes. :warning:

oliver: telemetry is key. add these events asap: `auth.claims.resolve`, `auth.attribution.override`, `quota.attribution.mismatch`. include fields: origin_project, effective_project, token_type, route_policy. example metric: `quota.attribution.mismatch.count` with tag mismatch=true.

platform-bot: deploy scheduled: auth-service v3.7.2 -> canary (region-us-west) by @dina in ~10m :rocket:

dina: rolling the header into mint service now. adding a small TTL to `x-origin-project` (24h) to avoid stale handoffs for long-lived tokens. also adding a unit test for double-resolution path.

samir: edge-case: what about delegated flows where the original project intentionally wants attribution to be the SA project (customer policy)? we need an opt-in flag at mint: `allow_attribution_override=true`. otherwise default should be preserved as origin.

jess: good call. default = preserve origin. add admin toggle in Console under Auth settings and a audit log entry when override is enabled.

leo: can we also emit a telemetry gauge for UI -> console banner impressions when mismatch occurs? helps measure confusion.

oliver: also add a short-lived artifact in logs so SREs can correlate: `auth: attribution(origin=A, effective=B, token=tokid123)` — searchable.

dina: test notes: reproducer script uses `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <delegated-token>"` to the /v1/chat endpoint. before patch, run `jq '.project'` on the quota worker logs to see misattribution. after patch, verify `x-origin-project` present and quota lines attribute to origin.

samir: can we avoid touching existing client SDKs? prefer server-side header injection at mint-time only. minimal API churn.

jess: yep. plan: (1) inject header at mint, (2) routing/quotas read header authoritative, (3) telemetry events, (4) console UI change + admin toggle, (5) rollout: canary -> 5% -> 25% -> global with automatic rollback on mismatch rate > 0.2%.

leo: i'll mock the console UI copy. short text: "Requests may be charged to the original project (origin) or the service account project (effective). Click to learn why."

platform-bot: canary finished: auth-service v3.7.2 -> 5% traffic. monitor `quota.attribution.mismatch.count` and `auth.claims.resolve.latency`.

jess: thanks all. i'll open a tiny RFC and add the rollout checklist. leaving notes for accounting and support so they can watch billing spikes. :thumbsup:

oliver: thanks — throwing a quick alert on the mismatch metric to pager-sre for the first 6 hours after each rollout step.

dina: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth/pull/462 — main change is header injection + tests. comments welcome.

samir: added a unit test case for opt-in override. LGTM.

jess: resolved for now, but will follow up if we see any more ghost-attribution. :eyes:
